value.rationale: The edge-budget spectral-gap optimization is a natural network robustness/mixing surrogate for a two-cycle-with-spokes graph family. The optimal n^-3 correction is an exact, nontrivial design invariant; the parity-dependent n^-2 coupling threshold comes from two competing long-wave Fourier degeneracies and explains when the inner jump-two network can receive almost the entire budget. Both scales furnish implementable edge-allocation design guidance, not merely reparameterization or routine table recomputation.
